text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: HydraCorp (dedicated-pool: hydra-prod-nyc) — elevated 95th percentile latency and token errors on model 'redwood-chat-xl-v3' across their dedicated GPUs. 5m window: 95p latency 3.2s (+150%), 5xx spike 3.4%. Impact: degraded response times and occasional truncated outputs. Page routed to oncall.

oncall-ryan: got the page, looking now. Any known deploys? @eng-sre-lina if you have quick telemetry pls.

eng-sre-lina: checking. No scheduled deploys in the last hour. I see sustained kernel queueing on node hydra-gpu-07 and a bunch of `kv_cache` misses. Errors originate in runtime shard r7.

eng-runtime-sam: tagging in — r7 has unusual memory churn with large sequences from HydraCorp. Might be a workload pattern change hitting our batching heuristics. Could be a recent prompt expansion from their side.

oncall-ryan: HydraCorp is on a dedicated pool (reserved). We need to avoid noisy-neighbor cross-tenant mitigation that could impact others. Propose two options: 1) apply a customer-scoped routing override to pin Hydra to a safe variant `redwood-chat-xl-v3-safe` (smaller context/quantized) OR 2) pin them to previous model build `redwood-chat-xl-v2` which historically had lower memory churn. Thoughts?

eng-sre-lina: prefer option 1 as it keeps them on latest behavior but forces a low-memory execution path. We can apply a transient override (5-30m) while we investigate. I'll run a targeted qps/latency check on hydra nodes.

eng-runtime-sam: We can flip a tenant override via admin API. Quick command:

```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/tenant-overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"hydra-corp","override": {"model":"redwood-chat-xl-v3-safe","reason":"latency spike 5m","expires_in_secs":900}}'
```

eng-runtime-sam: Policy JSON we would push (example):

```
{
  "tenant_id": "hydra-corp",
  "scope": "routing",
  "action": "force_model",
  "model": "redwood-chat-xl-v3-safe",
  "ttl": 900,
  "note": "auto-mitigation during observed latency/error spike"
}
```

account-exec-jiya: looping in customer contact. HydraOps (customer) needs status updates and confirmation that their data stays in dedicated pool and KMS remains local. Don't make changes that break their contract.

customer-ops-hydra: we see timeouts; thanks for the quick ping. We prefer pinning to a safe variant over rollback if it preserves output fidelity. Please confirm that requests won't leave our VPC or go to hosted fallbacks.

eng-sre-lina: confirmed — tenant-scoped overrides will not route traffic out of their dedicated pool. The override only changes the model binary used on their nodes. No cross-tenant routing.

security-ops: logging and audit trail required. If you push the override, add `audit_reason` and force retention for 90d. Also capture which operator applied it.

eng-runtime-sam: will include audit fields. Example flag: `audit_reason:"hydra-latency-1803456789"` and `operator:"oncall-ryan"`.

oncall-ryan: I'm going to apply the tenant override now for 15m to stabilize while Lina runs deeper diagnostics. I'll post exact command and TTL in the thread once done. Handing ops to @eng-sre-lina for follow-up monitoring — I'm available if escalation needed. :hand_off:

eng-sre-lina: watching tail of p95 and error-rate. If after 10m we don't see improvement we'll consider pin-to-v2 fallback.

oncall-ryan: override applied:

```
# applied at 1803456900
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/tenant-overrides -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant_id":"hydra-corp","override":{"model":"redwood-chat-xl-v3-safe","ttl":900,"audit_reason":"hydra-latency-1803456789","operator":"oncall-ryan"}}'
```

eng-sre-lina: initial effect: p95 drops from 3.2s -> 1.1s, 5xx spike drops to 0.1%. Good signal. We'll keep monitoring. Opening a runbook item to inspect kv_cache eviction pattern on r7.

customer-ops-hydra: thanks, that's a huge improvement. We'll run a few validation prompts and report any semantic regressions.

product-maria: keep me posted if there are any customer-visible regressions. If the safe variant changes output noticeably we may need to offer a staged canary with sampling (10% live) instead of full force.

eng-runtime-sam: noted — we can configure canary routing too, example policy: `force_model` with `sample_rate:0.1`.

security-ops: also ensure the override TTL is extended only via documented change and after account exec approval. No silent extensions.

account-exec-jiya: HydraOps confirmed OK with this temporary override and audit logging. They requested a post-incident note outlining root cause and any long-term mitigations.

eng-sre-lina: creating postmortem draft and adding artifact: per-node memory profiles, logs, and the override audit entry. Will include recommended safe-variant pins and kernel parameter tuning.

oncall-ryan: handing back to day oncall in 30m; if anything regresses tag me with `@oncall-ryan` and escalate to eng-runtime.

eng-runtime-sam: filing follow-up ticket to add tenant-specific auto-mitigation rule: if p95 > 2s and 5xx > 1% for 3 consecutive 1m windows, auto-apply safe-variant for 10m with audit. This will be gated by account exec opt-in.

customer-ops-hydra: appreciate it. Please include a contact SLA for follow-up and confirm no data egress. We'll validate outputs and revert when green.

eng-sre-lina: last check at 1803457890: stable. Closing the page but keeping the ticket open for root cause and remediation actions. :white_check_mark:

oncall-ryan: thanks team.
